abstract: On the truncated squarefree complex $C_x$ ($x\ge 2$) equipped with the boundary operator $d_x$ and Hermitian GCD overlap metric $G_{x,\rho}=C_{x,\rho}^* C_{x,\rho}$ ($|\rho_p|<1$), we study two finite-cutoff questions: when the Cholesky inverse overflow operator $M_{x,\rho}$ decays on sub-scales $C_y\subset C_x$, and how the conjugated boundary decomposes across quotient shells $S_n(x)=\{k:\lfloor x/k\rfloor=n\}$ and active cores $m=k_{\le n}\mid P_{\pi(n)}^\#$. First, we establish the dual Cartan overflow identities $L_x=S(x)I-T_x^* T_x$ and $L_{>x}=S(x)I-T_x T_x^*$, the order-ideal approximation residual for $G_{x,\rho}^{-1}$, and sufficient Rankin and Dirichlet-tail sub-scale decay bounds for $M_{x,\rho}M_{x,\rho}^*$ versus exponential $(1+\min(u_0,1))^{\pi(x)}-x$ divergence for constant overlaps $0<|\rho_0|<1$. Second, on each quotient shell $S_n(x)$, we prove that the active-core Buchstab-Mertens amplitude expands as $F(n;m;\gamma)=-\sum_{2\le d\le n\text{ sqfree},\gcd(d,m)=1}(-1)^{r_m(d)}\mu(d)\gamma(d)$, generating the prime-separation kernel $W(d_1,d_2)$. Re-indexing cores by their complement divisors $c=P_{\pi(n)}^\#/m$ makes the interior fiber map unimodular lower divisor-triangular with $\{-1,0,+1\}$-valued inverse and yields a closed-form interior inverse $(W_n^{\mathrm{int}})^{-1}$ that vanishes on all coprime pairs $\gcd(d_1,d_2)=1$, supplying pointwise fixed-$s$ coercivity bounds and support-preserving short-core estimates alongside the classical Montgomery-Vaughan vertical mean-value bound. No new zero-free region or proof of RH is claimed.
author: halasz_resonator
title: Quotient-Shell Prime-Separation Kernels, Unimodular Active-Core Inversion, and Sufficient Overflow Bounds in the Squarefree Complex
